subject: Revenue-share model for observability add-ons + SLA escrow
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Revenue-share alternative for observability add-ons + SLA escrow

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for an excellent demo last week. Based on the usage profile you shared (heavy tracing spikes during batch jobs + steady dashboard reads), I sketched an alternative commercial that may get us to procurement faster: a revenue-share option for the observability add-ons (retention + tracing + advanced dashboards) paired with an SLA escrow to cover retention/tracing SLOs.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Structure: 0 upfront commit for add-ons; Redwood receives a 6–10% revenue share on HearthTech’s subscription-derived incremental ARR attributable to AI/ops features for the first 18 months.
- Floor: If rev-share payments in a quarter fall below a guaranteed minimum (~$12k/month), HearthTech pays the difference as a committed monthly credit (protects unit economics).
- Escrow: 3 months of expected credit exposure placed into an escrow account; funds drawn only to satisfy SLA credits (retention/tracing availability / data durability).
- Term: 18 months, auto-evaluated at month 12 for conversion to a standard committed SKU or renewal of rev-share.
- Reporting: Monthly token/ingest/retention metrics to a shared dashboard; transparent math in the attached workbook.

Why this helps HearthTech: lowers procurement friction (no large upfront commitment), aligns incentives on adoption, and avoids over-provisioning for early-stage feature usage.

I attached a short SOW stub and an economics workbook that show sample math. If this looks promising, I can put together a one-page exhibit for procurement and loop legal on the escrow language.

Would you be open to reviewing that this week? Happy to do a 30-minute call to run through the numbers with Alex as well.

Best,
Hannah

--

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the creative structure — I like the flexibility. A few quick Qs from procurement/security: 
1) What counts as the "incremental ARR attributable to AI/ops features"? Is this based on usage signals or a product revenue allocation we must produce?
2) Can you confirm data residency implications of the dashboard/retention buckets (we need EU-only storage for certain datasets)?
3) How would the escrow be managed — does Redwood propose a third-party escrow agent or do you use a retained credit balance on the Redwood contract?

Also curious for an example: on the workbook, can you show a conservative adoption curve (month 1–6 low adoption) and what HearthTech would pay in months 1–6 vs. months 7–18? That will help the finance folks. Alex will join the next call.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director of Platform, HearthTech
sarah@hearthtech.com

On a related note — legal will want clear SLA triggers and a cap on credits so they can sign off quickly.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Revenue-share alternative for observability add-ons + SLA escrow

Forwarding Sarah's note — they like the idea but procurement/legal have three concrete asks (definition of incremental ARR, EU residency carveout, escrow mechanics). Can we agree internals on an opening position? My thoughts below.

Quick internal position (recommended):
- Definition: incremental ARR = uplift in subscription revenue attributable to features that rely on Redwood observability add-ons (dashboard seats + data-driven features). We measure via a simple attribution: flagged feature toggles + usage-based tieback (tokens + retention buckets). Workbook already contains two attribution models (conservative and aggressive).
- Data residency: offer EU-only retention buckets for regulated datasets — this maps to our Private deployment offering; attach a small per-GB differential. If they need entirely EU-hosted control plane + private deployment, we can toggle to Dedicated and reprice; keep rev-share only on EU-eligible usage in scope.
- Escrow: propose a third-party escrow (EscrowCo) or a short-term trust held by Redwood under a defined schedule. Legal will prefer an independent escrow agent; procurement will prefer retained credit. Suggest we offer both: independent escrow for enterprise legal, retained credit for faster signature.
- Floor math: set floor at $12k/month (18-month term) with a true-up every quarter.

Questions for Ben/Marissa/Laura: is the 6–10% rev-share range defensible to sales/legal? On our side we assume 8% mid-case. Also, how flexible are we on floor and escrow vendor?

I'll draft a 1-pager exhibit if we agree on the numbers.

--
Hannah

Thanks for the questions — attached is a concise exhibit and an updated SOW stub that reflect the items we discussed: attribution rules, EU carveout, and escrow options. Key changes vs. the first note: 
- Attribution: conservative model uses feature-flag + usage multiplier (sample included).
- Escrow options: (A) independent escrow agent (recommended for legal) or (B) retained credit on the Redwood account (faster); exhibit lists both flows and sample T+30 draw mechanics.
- Floor/fallback: $12k/month floor with quarterly true-up; after month 12 we can transition to committed SKU at a pre-agreed conversion discount.
- Example P&L: the workbook includes a 0–6 month conservative adoption curve and a 7–18 month ramp with line-item of what HearthTech would have paid under rev-share vs. a committed slab.

If you're good with the approach, next steps I suggest:
1) Set a 30-min procurement + legal sync (we'll bring contract exhibit and escrow terms)
2) If legal prefers escrow agent, we can loop in our commercial counsel and proposed agent (EscrowCo) and get a short pro-forma escrow agreement.
3) Parallel: we can lock in a tentative conversion discount now (e.g., 12% off list for conversion at month 12) to give HearthTech visibility.

I've attached: HearthTech_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW stub), obs_addons_revs_share_model.xlsx (workbook with conservative/adopt curves).

Would you like to lock a time tomorrow or Thursday for the legal/procurement sync?
